title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
description: You are given an uppercase string `s` and an integer `k`. You may change at most `k` characters of `s` to any other uppercase letter. Return the length of the longest substring made of one repeated letter after performing at most `k` changes.

examples.explanation: Change both X to Y (or both Y to X).
Change the B in "AAABA" to A.

constraints: s consists of uppercase English letters.
hints: For a fixed substring, how many changes are needed to make it uniform?
The cost is length minus the count of its most frequent letter. A window is acceptable when that cost is at most k.
Expand right and track letter counts and the max count seen; if length - max_count > k, advance left by one. The window never needs to shrink below its best size.

solution.explanation: Keep a sliding window and a count per letter, along with the highest count max_f seen in any window so far. The window is fixable when its length minus max_f is at most k. When it is not, move the left edge one step. Because max_f never needs to decrease, the window size only grows when a better answer exists, and the final window length is the result. Each index is processed once: O(n) time, O(26) space.
